newsitem.title: USA: O.J. Simpson lawyer takes British nanny case.
newsitem.headline: O.J. Simpson lawyer takes British nanny case.

text.p: Famed defence lawyer Barry Scheck appeared in court on Friday on behalf of a teenage British nanny charged with murder in the death of a Massachusetts infant in her care.
Scheck, part of the legal "dream team" who helped clear football star O.J. Simpson of two murder charges, was hired by the nanny's lawyers to use his forensic expertise in the case.
Louise Woodward, 19, of Chester, England, has been held without bail since February in the death of nine-month old Matthew Eappen.

Prosecuters have charged that Woodward, who has pled not guilty to first-degree murder charges, vigorously shook the baby to keep him from crying, then struck his head against a hard surface. If convicted of first-degree murder, Woodward faces life in prison with no chance of parole.

In a motion filed in court, Scheck said Woodward's lawyers have learned that the boy suffered from a genetic disorder, possibly one or two diseases which can lead to brain haemorrhages and false charges of child abuse.
Scheck, whose cutting inquiries of DNA tests are credited with tilting the jury in the Simpson case, was kept quiet in the Cambridge, Mass. court Friday.

Middlesex Superior Court Judge Hiller Zobel refused to allow Scheck to address the court, explaining that his application to the court to practice in the case was incomplete. Nevertheless, Scheck sat at the defence table next to Woodward and whispered advice to the defence lawyers.
In his motion, Scheck said that Eappen may have suffered from osteogenesis imperfecta or glutaric acidemia type one.
The trial is scheduled to start on August 11.
